values: Scenario and rules

The following training subjects, personnel codes, documents and rules are all editorially fictional and test material organisation only. Record table R3 serves as the checking baseline; record complete requires the score to reach the line, the reviewer to be present and the sign-off to be signed. A missing reviewer is judged to-check; other unmet conditions are judged to-supplement. Do not add a signature or change a score yourself.
Record table R3: subject A, 85 / line 80, reviewer A, signed; B, 77 / line 80, reviewer B, signed; C, 90 / line 85, reviewer blank, signed; D, 88 / line 85, reviewer D, not signed.

Summary S2: A signed; B score 82; C reviewer C; D signed. Compared against R3, there are only three differences: the B score, the C reviewer and the D sign-off. Dates: R3 and S2 are both fictional October 1; the version number identifies only the document and cannot be used to infer a real system.
Delivery tasks
Task one: list the three conflicts between S2 and R3 item by item, recording both original values, the checking baseline and the item to correct; keep the original text and do not delete S2.

Three conflicts: B 82 against 77, which should be recorded as 77 per R3; C reviewer C against blank, which should be recorded as reviewer to-check rather than guessing C; D signed against not signed, which should be recorded as not signed per R3. The original S2 record is retained and the correction is recorded separately with a version and reason.

subject.name: Artillery and missile officers
subject.summary: Under US O*NET 55-1014.00, artillery and missile officers manage personnel and weapon operations, with duties covering coordination of field / air defence artillery deployment, fire control communications, intercontinental ballistic missile aiming and launching, storage and handling of nuclear ammunition and components, security of weapon storage and launch facilities, and weapon system maintenance. It is a broad occupational classification, does not mean every officer carries out all duties, and cannot be summarised as only ground indirect fire.
